audit_items.proof_trace: `burn_ctokens` computes `redeem_collateral_amount = exchange_rate.int_mul(ctokens.value())` where `int_mul` is defined as `floor(rate.value * ctokens / WAD)`, yielding a u64. The strict equality `coin_received == exchange_rate * ctokens` does not hold when the product is non-integer, but the deviation is at most 1 unit per withdrawal (floor truncation), which stays in the pool benefiting remaining depositors — this is standard fixed-point arithmetic, not an exploitable accounting error. All withdrawal paths go through this single function, and `accrue_interest` is always called first in `handle_withdraw`, ensuring the rate is fresh.
